technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring Boot 3.x with Java 17+ as the base framework for all new modules and CI infrastructure.
Leverage Spring Cloud Stream for building streaming modules and integrating with external systems like Redis and HDFS.
Implement REST APIs using Spring MVC and Spring WebFlux for both synchronous and asynchronous operations.
Use Maven as the build tool for dependency management and CI pipeline integration.
Adopt Spring Boot's auto-configuration and externalized configuration for the ModuleLauncher bootification.
Integrate with existing XD components where applicable, ensuring backward compatibility during migration.
Use embedded servers (e.g., Tomcat) for standalone deployment scenarios.
Apply modular design principles to separate concerns between StreamController, ModuleLauncher, and individual modules.
assumptions: Developers have prior experience with Spring ecosystem, Java 17+, and Maven.
Existing repositories (s-c-d, s-c-s-m) are accessible and have basic build configurations in place.
CI infrastructure will be set up using GitHub Actions or Jenkins, with standard plugins and configurations.
External dependencies (e.g., Redis, HDFS) are available for testing and integration.
ModuleLauncher bootification will follow standard Spring Boot conventions without major architectural changes.
REST support for stream commands will be implemented using existing StreamController endpoints.
PHD porting investigation will be limited to dependency analysis and proof-of-concept implementation.
All user stories are independent and can be developed in parallel where possible.
